Subject: Post-demo follow-up: Monarch Health SLOs, streaming & concurrency

Hi Alicia / Platform team — thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single place to iterate from.

Recap (what we heard you need)
- Latency: 95th percentile goal ~750ms for patient triage responses (typical payloads ~80-160 tokens).
- Throughput: average sustained ~30 RPS; expected peak bursts up to ~110 RPS during morning shifts.
- Concurrency / connections: streaming-enabled chat clients, long-lived HTTP/2 connections. You expect ~500 concurrently open streams across the fleet during peak and roughly 10–15 active streams per app instance.
- Streaming behavior: partial tokens for progressive UI; want low tail latency for first-byte.
- Safety/observability: audit logs + request tracing are required for initial pilot.

Open questions we promised to answer
1) Recommended initial rate limits and connection-pool sizing for pilot.
2) How Redwood handles backpressure and soft throttling vs hard rate limit responses.
3) Whether a Dedicated pool is recommended given the burst profile and 95th SLO.

Attachments: monarch_algo_requirements.pdf (your doc), Redwood_SLA-template.docx (initial SLA draft).

Proposed next steps
- We’ll propose an initial quota table and connection-pool config for pilot by EOD Monday.
- Schedule a 30–45m capacity call with your infra team to walk through long-lived streaming semantics and fallbacks (Ben + Marissa to join).
- Share a small test plan for ramping traffic (smoke → ramp → production).

If the above matches your notes, I’ll send the quota suggestion and calendar invites.

Thanks,
Hannah

Hi Hannah — thanks for the succinct recap. Confirming details from our side and adding a few clarifications from infra:

Confirmed numbers (from product/ops)
- Sustained: 25–35 RPS for baseline daytime operations.
- Bursts: up to ~115 RPS for short windows (1–3 minutes) during shift change and scheduled notifications.
- Concurrent open streams: platform team observed ~450–550 concurrent long-lived streams during our internal load tests.
- Avg response size: ~120 tokens; some clinical workflows return up to 500 tokens but those are rarer.

Streaming/connection expectations
- We use HTTP/2 long-lived streams (server push not used). We expect Redwood to support streaming partial tokens over the same stream and maintain idle connections for ~2–3 minutes before idle close.
- We plan to multiplex up to 12 logical chat sessions per app worker process, which maps to ~8–12 concurrent streams per instance.

Rate-limit behavior & backpressure
- If Redwood returns 429/429 Retry-After, we will implement exponential backoff with jitter. We prefer a soft-throttle approach (early warning headers) over immediate hard drops for user-facing sessions.

Security/observability
- We will need per-request IDs to correlate logs, and access to the audit logs for the pilot window.

Action items for Redwood
- Please share a recommended starting quota (RPS + burst window + connection-pool size) and an initial SLA proposal.
- Can you indicate whether Dedicated capacity would be required to meet 95th 750ms SLO for the burst profile?

Alicia
Alicia Gomez
Head of Product Integrations, Monarch Health

Subject: RE: Post-demo follow-up: Monarch Health SLOs, streaming & concurrency

Quick internal note / draft proposal before we send to Alicia:

Initial quota suggestion (pilot) — conservative, removable after pilot metrics
- Global sustained RPS: 40 RPS (soft limit)
- Burst allowance: up to 120 RPS with a 90s burst window and token-bucket smoothing
- Concurrent streaming connections: soft limit 600 open streams, with a hard cap at 750 to protect shared pools
- Per-API-key concurrency: recommend 20 parallel token-generation requests maximum
- Idle connection timeout: 180s (configurable)

Rationale
- The sustained 40 RPS gives a buffer above their baseline and lets us observe behavior. Burst up to 120 RPS maps to their worst-case while smoothing avoids sudden hard-failures.
- Concurrent stream soft-limit at 600 supports their 450–550 peak with headroom.
- Per-key concurrency prevents noisy neighbors; 20 should cover multiplexing 8–12 sessions per process while allowing some parallel calls (rerank, embeddings).

SLO guidance and capacity recommendation
- Given the 95th 750ms target with bursty peaks, we should recommend Redwood Dedicated for the initial pilot window. Dedicated pool reduces tail spikes and gives us control over kernel/packing decisions for streaming.

Next steps (internal -> send to Monarch)
1) Hannah: send proposed quota table + SLA draft to Alicia, link Drive folder, propose capacity call slots next Tue/Wed.
2) Marissa: prepare a short capacity runbook for the call (what metrics we’ll look at, failure modes).
3) If Alicia signs off, spin up a 1–2 GPU Dedicated pilot profile for 2 weeks and run staged ramp.

Thoughts?
-ben
Ben Carter
